summary.text: Observed synthetic 300 rpm trial: stopping at second 60 yielded final-vial attenuations 0.204, 0.209, 0.207, approximately 2.4 percent spread. This once meets the at-most-4-percent sample proxy and counters universal necessity of sustained 900 rpm and stable optical checks. Repeatability and time savings remain unknown.

Proposed intervention, with success hypothetical: six fresh trials in three fixed-duration 300/900 rpm pairs, exactly 60 stirring seconds, no optical-controlled restart. Alternate speed and depth-sampling orders; fix 150 mL water, 0.30 mL dye, addition location, bottle, rinsed vessel, camera and references. Log five-second images through second 120, then withdraw 1 mL at 10, 28, 45 mm within ten seconds. Report raw vials, spreads, duration and every failure. Use spill tray; stop if liquid escapes.

Hypothesis: agitation creates image disturbances despite achievable sample uniformity; predict both speeds meet final target while larger 900 rpm image fluctuations decline after stopping. Rival hypothesis: genuine gradients dominate or the lower-speed success was exceptional; predict repeated 300 rpm sample failures and 900 rpm successes, with persistent spread tracking failure. Mixed outcomes remain unresolved. Specks and cessation responses cannot identify bubbles or establish uniformity during stirring.

residue.text: Deferred source proposal: compare enabled 900 rpm optical rule with a timer-stopped 60-second 900 rpm trial, logging shadow decisions; cap both by second 105 and sample at 120. Hypothesis: both succeed but timer control reduces stirring. Rival: extra stirring improves final samples. Fixed pairs alone cannot establish actual feedback prolongation; unequal quiet durations confound attribution. This requires a separate allocation within six trials.

Deferred source proposal: reverse-order speed pairs with matched stir-off interval at seconds 45–50, resume and stop at 65 for 60 total stirring seconds. Outcomes remain hypothetical; settling and surface changes complicate interpretation. This cannot be added beyond the six-trial allocation.

Preserved limits: matched 900 rpm final-vial evidence is absent; rpm is commanded only. Sampling and transfers can disturb gradients. Common-aliquot repeatability is not calibration; bubble fraction and absolute concentration are unmeasurable. Limited replication and order effects constrain inference. Other fluids, vessels and continuous operation remain untested; no real chemical or human benefit follows.

Case option omitted from this construction: syringe low-to-high bulk redistribution is available, but no successful outcome is observed. Any proposed combination with rotation would be a new hypothesis and transfers could disturb gradients.
